newsitem.title: GERMANY: Reuters German Advertising & Media Digest - Apr 23.
newsitem.headline: Reuters German Advertising & Media Digest - Apr 23.

text.p: REUTERS GERMAN ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST
News from Reuters and the German press on Advertising, Marketing, Media and the Internet
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:
KRONBERG, Germany - The growth of the German advertising market is slowing down, says media marketing company IP Deutschland.

The firm forecasts that net spending for media, cinema and billboard advertising will increase by only 1.9 percent to 32.8 billion marks, below the 2.5 economic growth which the government predicts for 1997. (Reuter)
FRANKFURT - The decision by London-based advertising and marketing group Cordiant Plc to demerge into three independently managed businesses is welcomed by two of its German ad units.
Directors of agencies Bates and Scholz & Friends say the Cordiant dissolution will boost growth by freeing them to compete and respond to client needs more effectively. (Reuter)
MEDIA & THE INTERNET:

HAMBURG - Deutsche Telekom chairman Ron Sommer says the telecommunications giant is ready for concessions over the use by other companies of its cable network. Sommer's comments come ahead of a high-level conference to be held next month, set to be a last-ditch bid to break a deadlock over the expansion of German cable television networks and the introduction of broadscale digital TV programming, which industry squabbling has held up for nearly two years. (Reuter)

FRANKFURT - German media companies and publishers are spending an increasing amount of money on consumer market research, says the Working Group of Market and Social Research Institutes (ADM). Media companies and publishers accounted for 17 percent of market research contracts last year, up from 12 percent in 1995. (Reuter)

FRANKFURT - Head of Pro Sieben Digital Media GmbH, Karlheinz Jungbeck, takes up the postion of chairman of the German Television Research Working Group (AGF) after his predecessor Kurt Ludwig switches from Sat 1 to the media agency HMS Carat.
(Horizont)

HAMBURG - German subscription channel Premiere wants to extend its digital test programming until the end of the year, before deciding whether to expand the project. Premiere said a survey of digital customers showed great satisfaction with the service, broadcast since March. (Reuter)
BERLIN - Private German channel Sat 1 will start publishing a quarterly company newsletter called "Profile" in April for advertising clients, firms, politicians and journalists.
(Reuter)
PEOPLE NEWS:

HAMBURG - German subscription channel Premiere fills two top jobs. From May 1 Barbara Gauer, currently public relations head at the Cologne production company CreaTV, will take over as head of programme communications. Former Pro Sieben journalist Winka Wulff will take over as head of the Fiction & Entertainment co-production for Premiere Productions from June 1. (Reuter)
